cited_validation_literature.citation: Mose T et al. (2012). Meta-analysis of data from human ex vivo placental perfusion studies on genotoxic and immunotoxic agents within the integrated European project NewGeneris. Placenta 33(5):433–439.
cited_validation_literature.reviewed_access: PubMed and University of Copenhagen abstracts; full text and any supplemental files not reviewed.
cited_validation_literature.reported_outcome_summary: Abstract describes re-analysis of thirteen agents across three ex vivo laboratories. Antipyrine transfer differed between studies/labs; normalization reduced variance, but the abstract says the correction only partially addresses small methodological differences and transfer rankings vary slightly by endpoint.
cited_validation_literature.evidence_role: Cross-laboratory method-comparison context. Distinct compounds/endpoints from the 2020 hormone/amino-acid workbook; not eligible for pooling with it or as gestational support evidence.
cited_validation_literature.data_discovery_status: No row-level dataset linked from the PubMed or institutional records inspected; this does not establish that no supplementary or separately published records exist.
cited_validation_literature.intake_status: Context only; retain normalization and recovery limitations, do not transcribe aggregate rankings as individual observations.

cited_validation_literature.citation: Karttunen V et al. (2015). Criteria and challenges of the human placental perfusion—Data from a large series of perfusions. Toxicology in Vitro 29(7):1482–1491.
cited_validation_literature.reviewed_access: PubMed abstract; full text and any supplemental files not reviewed.
cited_validation_literature.reported_outcome_summary: Abstract describes more than one hundred perfusions from one center since 2005. Gestational duration over 40 weeks was associated with a lower fetomaternal antipyrine ratio; placental weight and delivery mode did not affect the reported success criteria. The authors identify possible recovery loss to perfusion-system materials as a study concern.
cited_validation_literature.evidence_role: Single-center assay-throughput and covariate context; not a developmental outcome or a whole-gestation result.
cited_validation_literature.data_discovery_status: No row-level dataset linked from the PubMed record inspected; this does not establish that no supplementary or separately published records exist.
cited_validation_literature.intake_status: Context only; do not pool counts or success rates across laboratories without aligned eligibility definitions.

cited_validation_literature.reviewed_access: PubMed abstract; full text and any supplemental files not reviewed.
cited_validation_literature.reported_outcome_summary: Abstract reports 89 collected placentas and 34 meeting the study's antipyrine and quality-control success criteria (38%).
cited_validation_literature.evidence_role: A separate laboratory's implementation and assay-yield context; not evidence of embryonic development or gestational support.
cited_validation_literature.data_discovery_status: No row-level dataset linked from the PubMed record inspected; this does not establish that no supplementary or separately published records exist.
cited_validation_literature.intake_status: Context only; retain as a distinct cohort and do not combine its yield with the 2010 Copenhagen or Kuopio counts.

cited_validation_literature.citation: Schneider H et al. (2022). Ex vivo dual perfusion of an isolated human placenta cotyledon: Towards protocol standardization and improved inter-centre comparability. Placenta 126:83–89.
cited_validation_literature.reviewed_access: Publisher abstract and search-indexed open-access PDF record; direct PDF retrieval failed, so full text was not verified.
cited_validation_literature.reported_scope: The abstract identifies broad inter-centre variation in establishment, perfusate composition, gas conditions, cannulation method, flow, perfused tissue mass and quality-control practice. It proposes a multi-centre pilot to examine effects on placental function and structure; this paper is a standardization rationale, not the pilot's outcome report.
cited_validation_literature.evidence_role: Candidate comparability-factor source for isolated placenta assays; no direct gestational-support or embryo-outcome evidence.
cited_validation_literature.data_discovery_status: No linked row-level dataset or completed pilot results identified from the abstract and records inspected.
cited_validation_literature.intake_status: Use listed categories as candidate metadata prompts only; not a validated minimum reporting standard or a source for protocol setpoints.

cited_validation_literature.citation: Glättli SC et al. (2024). Variability in perfusion conditions and set-up parameters used in ex vivo human placenta models: A literature review. Placenta 157:37–49.
cited_validation_literature.reviewed_access: PubMed abstract, full open-access publisher PDF hosted by the University of Groningen, and five publisher supplementary DOCX files. Table structure and phase headings inspected; study-specific setup values were not added to this intake.
cited_validation_literature.reported_scope: Review searched PubMed through 2022-09-26 and included 135 studies (2000–2022) of therapeutic drug transfer in uncomplicated full-term placentae with fixed within-run setup. It reports substantial inter-laboratory differences and says studies are not readily comparable or interchangeable.
cited_validation_literature.reporting_completeness_summary: The review says 65.8% of setup parameters were present in primary reports, another 13.6% could be recovered from cited protocols, and 20.6% remained undescribed even after that search; it also notes some cited protocol information was inconsistent.
cited_validation_literature.data_discovery_status: S2-S5 are per-study setup metadata tables grouped by phase/direction. The review explicitly excluded measurement outcomes from extraction. Structure/headings inspected only; no setup values were imported.
cited_validation_literature.evidence_role: Evidence-intake and missingness context for drug-transfer methods; not a completed inter-centre pilot and not gestational-development evidence.
cited_validation_literature.intake_status: Candidate source for metadata vocabulary only; do not pool its therapeutic-drug setup records with the 2020 hormone/amino-acid observations.
